name: doctor: read-only coherence and drift report
description:
Split out of the sync/doctor task so the read-only half lands first and can be pointed at the live machine safely.

gitfriend doctor inspects and reports; it NEVER writes. Exits non-zero if any problem is found, zero otherwise, so it can gate the cutover.

Checks:
- config coherence: defaults.account names a declared account; every match pattern compiles; no two accounts claim the same pattern (which would make resolution ambiguous at run time)
- secrets: every declared secret variable has a stored value, reported by fingerprint or as MISSING
- ambient exposure: managed variables currently present in the environment. This is the condition the project exists to remove, so seeing it reported is the before-picture of the cutover
- git wiring: credential.helper mentions gitfriend, and credential.useHttpPath is true for github.com - without the latter the org never reaches the helper and every github account resolves identically

Never prints a token value, only fingerprints (R10, R12).

Acceptance criteria:
- a clean fixture reports no problems and exits zero
- each check fails the way it should on a deliberately broken fixture
- running it against the real machine config is safe and changes nothing
result:
Read-only doctor done. 45 tests pass, clippy clean. Validated against the REAL machine using a draft config in a scratchpad; nothing in HOME was touched.

Checks: config coherence (default names a declared account, patterns compile, no two accounts claim the same pattern), secret presence by fingerprint or MISSING, ambient exposure, and git wiring (helper mentions gitfriend, useHttpPath true for github.com). Exits non-zero on any problem so it can gate the cutover.

useHttpPath unset is graded a PROBLEM not a warning: without it the helper is only ever asked about github.com, so all three GitHub accounts resolve identically. Total and silent failure.

BUG FOUND BY RUNNING IT FOR REAL: ambient variables were reported per account, so GH_TOKEN appeared three times. Now deduped per variable. Worth noting the first regression test PASSED VACUOUSLY because the fixture had only one account declaring GH_TOKEN; rewritten with two accounts, it then failed as it should before the fix.

LIVE FINDINGS from the preview run, all new information:

1. credential.helper resolves to FOUR helpers: osxkeychain, manager, and git-credential-manager twice. osxkeychain was NOT visible in ~/.gitconfig-common - it comes from a system-level gitconfig. The cutover has more to untangle than reading the user file suggested.

2. Both GH_TOKEN and GITEA_TOKEN are currently set in the ambient environment, confirming the exposure this project targets, live.

3. REQUIREMENTS.md IS WRONG ABOUT DIGILOPE. It states Digilope uses ssh remotes with no token in the push/pull path. In fact two hostnames are in use - app-gitea.digilope.com over ssh AND gitea.digilope.com over HTTPS - and simple-schematic exists twice, once via each. So Digilope DOES need a token for git transport, and gitAuth is a property of a remote rather than of an account. Recorded for the cutover.

4. The KitchenCloud nesting hazard DISAPPEARS under URL matching, as predicted: all five repos are github.com/KitchenCloudDev/*, so the org distinguishes them and declaration order stops mattering. Path rules are still needed there because two repos (_jjscopetest, kitchen-cloud-reactnative) have NO remote at all - the R4 case, live.

5. ~/Developer/Profound spans SEVEN orgs: DanielAtProfound, profoundcollective, profound-rj, EJ-Rice, AquaTraction, Composite-Labs, KitchenCloudDev.

6. UNRESOLVED ISSUE, needs a decision before cutover: ~12 third-party clones live under ~/Developer/DanielCarmingham (microsoft, dotnet, charmbracelet, ghostty-org, ...) plus one under Digilope. Their remotes match NO account pattern. Today path rules give them the personal identity. Under URL matching resolve_repo returns NoMatch, an ERROR, so gitfriend exec would fail in them. Options: let an unmatched remote fall back to the default tagged with a distinct Unmatched reason so callers can decide, or require explicit patterns. The credential helper must keep refusing either way (R11). Not changed here.

Verification evidence:
- clean fixture reports no problems and exits zero. PASS
- missing secret, undeclared default, duplicate pattern, foreign credential helper, useHttpPath off: each fails the way it should. PASS
- ambient check names the variable and never the value. PASS
- shared variable reported once. PASS after fix
- real-machine run is read-only and exits 1 with an accurate report. PASS

name: Track token expiry and warn before it lapses
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-10 against the real machine, no longer a lead.

MECHANISM: one authenticated request to https://api.github.com/user returns the header

    github-authentication-token-expiration: 2026-12-16 04:00:00 UTC

for tokens that have an expiry. Confirmed for fine-grained PATs (github_pat_ prefix).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT, also verified: OAuth tokens (gho_ prefix, what gh auth login produces) return NO expiry header at all - they return x-oauth-scopes instead, because they do not expire. So absence of the header means "does not expire", NOT an error or an unknown. Getting that wrong would make every gh-issued token look broken.

BIGGER FINDING, and probably the better feature: the same request VALIDATES the token. GH_TOKEN_DanielCarmingham on this machine returns 401 Bad credentials while GH_TOKEN_DanielAtProfound returns 200 - a dead credential sitting in the environment, unnoticed. That is precisely the silent failure this project exists to remove, and checking validity is more valuable than checking expiry since it catches revocation, not just lapse. Same request answers both.

Suggested shape:
- doctor grows a --check-remote or similar flag. NOT default: it makes network calls with real credentials, and doctor is currently offline and instant. Keep the fast offline path as the default.
- Per token: valid / invalid / expires in N days / does not expire.
- Never print the token; the login the token maps to is safe and useful to show, since it confirms the account mapping end to end.
- Gitea and GitLab have equivalent self endpoints; check what expiry metadata each returns.

Storing an expiry alongside the secret is then optional rather than necessary - asking beats remembering, because a token rotated outside gitfriend would leave stored metadata stale. Only store it if the offline path needs to warn without network.

Acceptance: doctor --check-remote reports valid/invalid and days-to-expiry per account, treats a missing expiry header as "does not expire", and prints no token material.

name: GitHub: short-lived tokens instead of long-lived PATs
description:
UNVERIFIED LEADS - confirm against current docs before planning.

GitHub is the one provider where rotation is the wrong frame. There is deliberately no API to mint a PAT, so the answer is not to rotate PATs faster but to stop using them.

Two candidate directions:

- GITHUB APP INSTALLATION TOKENS. An app private key signs a JWT, which is exchanged for an installation token that expires in about an hour. Fully automatable, and the long-lived secret becomes a private key that never leaves the machine rather than a token that is sent to a server on every request. Fits gitfriend well: the credential helper is invoked per operation and could mint on demand and cache briefly. Cost: an app has to be created and installed per org, which is real setup for three accounts.

- OAUTH DEVICE FLOW, which is what gh auth login already does. Yields a refreshable token. Lower setup cost, but it is a user-level grant rather than a per-account one, and this project exists precisely because gh has no per-repository account binding - so check carefully whether the token can be scoped per account before assuming it helps.

Worth noting the current setup ALREADY depends on gh auth git-credential for github.com, so the OAuth path is closer to where the machine is today than it first appears.

Fine-grained PATs are the middle option: still manually created, but they carry an expiry, so they at least interact well with the expiry-tracking task rather than lasting forever.

Decide the direction before writing anything. The installation-token route changes what a GitHub account IS in accounts.toml - a key and an app id rather than a token variable - so it is a schema question, not just an adapter.

name: Wrap provider MCP servers
description:
Implement gitfriend mcp sync: rewrite provider MCP entries in .mcp.json so command launches through gitfriend exec, which resolves the account from the servers working directory at launch and injects only that accounts variables.

Example rewrite - command becomes gitfriend, args become ["exec", "--", "<original command>", "<original args...>"]. No secret value is ever written into .mcp.json, which is frequently committed.

Fix Digilope/one-drop-visuals FIRST - it is the live exposure case: it runs gitea-mcp with an empty env block today, inheriting whatever credential happened to be ambient when Claude Code launched. Nine repos under ~/Developer have a .mcp.json; only that one currently runs a provider MCP.

doctor must flag any provider MCP still running unwrapped, so a newly added one cannot regress silently.

Acceptance criteria:
- gitea-mcp in one-drop-visuals authenticates as Digilope with no GH_TOKEN present in its environment
- rewriting is idempotent and preserves unrelated servers (filesystem, playwright, sequential-thinking) untouched
- doctor detects a hand-added unwrapped provider MCP
result:
MCP wrapping done. 55 tests pass, clippy clean. Dry-run verified against the real machine; nothing was written.

gitfriend mcp sync <paths...> rewrites a provider servers command so it launches through gitfriend exec, which resolves the account from the servers working directory and injects only that accounts variables. Reports and stops by default; --write applies.

KEY DECISION: wrap the command rather than write an env block. These files are usually committed, so a token in one would be a secret in version control (R10). The wrapper carries no value at all.

Three properties pinned by tests, all mattering because these files are committed and hand-edited:
- IDEMPOTENT. sync gets re-run whenever a server is added; a second pass must be a no-op or the command grows another "exec --" prefix each time. Detection keys off the ARGUMENT SHAPE gitfriend writes, not the command path, which varies by install location.
- ORDER-PRESERVING. serde_json pulled in with the preserve_order feature so keys keep their positions. Without it a one-line change becomes a whole-file diff for a human to review.
- NARROW. Only servers whose command or args carry a known provider marker (gitea-mcp, forgejo-mcp, github-mcp, gitlab-mcp, server-github, server-gitlab, server-gitea) are touched. filesystem, playwright and sequential-thinking are left byte-identical.

Verification evidence:
- wraps a gitea server into gitfriend exec -- <original command> <original args>. PASS
- non-provider servers untouched. PASS
- wrapping twice produces an identical file and reports no changes. PASS
- key order survives, asserted on the rendered text. PASS
- unwrapped_servers() reports the exposure without changing anything. PASS
- LIVE DRY RUN across three real .mcp.json files: correctly identifies Digilope/one-drop-visuals as the only one needing a change, and reports nothing to change for bmap and profound-automation. PASS
- applied to a COPY of the real file and diffed: only the gitea server changed, "type" and every other server preserved. PASS

NOT done:
- The real file has NOT been rewritten. That is a cutover action.
- doctor does not yet call unwrapped_servers - it has no list of .mcp.json paths to scan. In the meantime "mcp sync" without --write IS the check, and reports exactly the same thing. Wiring it into doctor needs a decision about where the list of paths comes from (scan ~/Developer, or declare roots in accounts.toml).
- The wrapped command records the path of the binary that ran sync. During the cutover this must be the INSTALLED path, not a target/debug build, or the config breaks as soon as the build directory is cleaned.

name: exec wrapper and CLI shims
description:
Implement gitfriend exec [--account X] -- cmd ... : resolve the account, scrub every provider variable inherited from the parent environment, then inject only the resolved account variables into that one child process.

Scrubbing is the R11 guarantee: a stale ambient GH_TOKEN must not survive into a Gitea child. Scrub first, then populate - never merge.

Generate shims on PATH for gh and tea (and glab / az devops once installed) that forward to gitfriend exec. Shims are a convenience layer; exec is the mechanism.

Note tea has never been logged in on this machine (~/.config/tea does not exist), so the Gitea CLI path needs a first-run setup as part of validating this.

Acceptance criteria:
- with a hostile GH_TOKEN pre-set in the parent shell, the child of a Gitea account does not see it (R11)
- gh api user --jq .login reports the right login from a repo under each GitHub account
- exec refuses, non-zero, when the resolved account declares a variable with no backing secret (R8) - and emits no other account token
result:
exec wrapper and shim generation done. 32 tests pass, clippy clean.

gitfriend exec [--account X] -- cmd... resolves the account from the working repo, clears every managed variable, then sets the resolved account variables, and runs the command inheriting nothing else. gitfriend shim install --dir DIR gh tea generates wrapper scripts.

KEY DESIGN DECISION: the scrub set comes from the WHOLE CONFIG, not from the account being run. That direction is the point - an account knows what it needs, not what it must be protected from. A Gitea account never mentions GH_TOKEN, which is exactly why an inherited GH_TOKEN would otherwise survive into it. Consequence: adding an account automatically protects every other account from it, with no per-account deny lists to maintain.

Literal entries (VAR=value, e.g. GITEA_HOST) pass through unchanged; bare names (GH_TOKEN) are fetched from the secret backend.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE CREDENTIAL PATH, deliberate: exec ALLOWS a Default resolution where the credential helper refuses it. Running gh outside any repo should use the declared default; refusing there would be hostile rather than safe. The dangerous cases still fail loudly - a repo whose remote matches no account errors rather than falling back, and a declared variable with no stored value refuses rather than running the command with a gap the CLI would fill from elsewhere.

Shims bake in the wrapped binary absolute path rather than re-resolving at run time: the script stays readable, and a stale path is something doctor can detect whereas a recursion loop is not. Binary resolution also skips the shim directory itself, so a shim cannot find itself.

Verification evidence:
- injects the declared variables for the resolved account. PASS
- variables belonging to OTHER accounts appear in the scrub set. PASS, R11
- a variable that is both scrubbed and needed ends up set - order is clear-then-populate. PASS
- literal VAR=value passes through unchanged. PASS
- missing secret refuses, naming account and variable. PASS, R8
- END-TO-END: hostile GH_TOKEN set in the parent shell, real binary run from a Gitea repo, child environment inspected via /usr/bin/env: the hostile token is absent and GITEA_TOKEN is present. PASS, R11
- END-TO-END through a GENERATED SHIM: same result. PASS

NOT done: gh api user --jq .login against the live machine, since that needs real tokens imported - that is the secret CLI and cutover work. Nothing on this machine has been changed.

name: Resolver core: accounts.toml + resolution algorithm
description:
Build the pure resolution layer that every other subcommand calls. No secrets, no side effects.

Modules: config.rs (serde/toml load + validate of accounts.toml), resolve.rs (the algorithm), git.rs (thin wrapper over git config / rev-parse).

Algorithm, in order:
1. URL given: match host+path against each account match glob; longest match wins; a tie between two accounts is a hard error.
2. No URL but cwd is a repo: read remote.origin.url, then go to step 1. Non-origin remotes are ignored for identity.
3. Repo with no origin: longest-prefix match on the paths list.
4. Nothing matched: the explicitly declared defaults.account.

Returns Resolved { account, reason } where reason is UrlMatch | OriginUrl | PathFallback | Default. The reason field is what makes R8 enforceable downstream: callers refuse to hand over a secret on a Default resolution unless the account really is the declared default.

Hermetic test harness: temp HOME, fixture repos, no real tokens, no network.

Acceptance criteria - tests map 1:1 onto requirements:
- R1/R2: a clone at /tmp/anywhere and a linked worktree in a foreign root both resolve correctly
- R3: github.com/DanielCarmingham/x and github.com/EJ-Rice/y resolve to different accounts from identical cwds
- R4: git init with no remote resolves via paths, then default, with the correct reason set
- DanielAtKitchenCloud nested inside ~/Developer/Profound/ resolves by longest prefix
- fork case: origin=personal, upstream=work resolves to personal
result:
Resolver core built test-first. 10 tests, all passing; clippy clean on --all-targets.

Modules: config.rs (accounts.toml, deny_unknown_fields so a mistyped key errors rather than being ignored), git.rs (shells out to git for remote.origin.url), resolve.rs (the four-step chain).

Resolution order, each answer tagged with a Reason: origin URL match, then longest path prefix for remote-less repos, then the declared default. Reason is UrlMatch | OriginUrl | PathFallback | Default so callers can refuse to release a secret on a low-confidence Default (R8).

Two decisions worth recording:
- Matching picks the MOST SPECIFIC pattern, scored by how many characters it pins literally, not the first declared. This removes the declaration-ordering trap the includeIf gitdir rules have, where a nested org only resolves correctly if its rule comes last.
- An equally-specific match on two different accounts is a hard error naming both, never a pick. Matching several of one accounts own patterns is not ambiguity.

URL normalization reduces all three shapes git accepts (https, ssh:// with optional port, scp-style host:path) to one host/path form. The scheme is what disambiguates a port from an scp separator, so the colon is only rewritten when no scheme was present.

Verification evidence:
- R1/R2 relocated clone: repo in a temp dir, outside every account root, resolves by origin. PASS
- R2 linked worktree in a foreign root: PASS. Confirmed by hand that the worktrees .git is a FILE containing a gitdir: pointer, so the test is not vacuous - path-based logic genuinely cannot resolve it.
- R3 two orgs on one host resolve to different accounts. PASS
- R4 no remote falls through path rule then declared default, with the reason set accordingly. PASS
- Nested-org specificity (Profound-Kitchen inside Profound-*) resolves regardless of declaration order. PASS
- Ambiguous equal-specificity match errors naming both candidates. PASS
- Fork with origin=personal, upstream=work resolves to personal. PASS

Honest note on TDD: the linked-worktree and fork tests passed on first run - they guard behaviour that asking git already provided, rather than driving new code. The other tests each failed for their intended reason first.

Not done here, deliberately: main.rs is still a stub, since subcommand dispatch belongs with the credential helper.

name: sync and doctor: generate gitconfigs, report drift
description:
Narrowed: doctor split into its own task (74hwdycd) so the read-only half could land first. This task is now the WRITING half.

gitfriend sync generates, into clearly marked generated regions:
- ~/.gitconfig-<Account> per account (user.name, user.email, core.sshcommand for ssh accounts)
- the includeIf hasconfig:remote.*.url: block in ~/.gitconfig-common, replacing the includeIf gitdir: rules

Then retire the superseded machinery: delete the account block from ~/.config/direnv/direnvrc and the token exports from the account-root .envrc files. direnv goes back to being only project environments.

THE HAZARD, verified by reading the file: ~/.gitconfig-common sets credential.helper FOUR times including two empty resets, and currently routes github.com through git-credential-manager. gitfriend must displace GCM for github.com while leaving it for other hosts, and credential.useHttpPath must be set true for github.com or the org never reaches the helper. Untangle that stack before switching anything.

Transcribe real emails, match patterns and ssh key paths from the existing ~/.gitconfig-Github-* and ~/.gitconfig-Digilope-Gitea-Daniel files - the values in the design doc are illustrative placeholders.

Editing files in HOME requires the cfg bare repo invocation (git --git-dir=/Users/daniel/.cfg --work-tree=/Users/daniel), and git add needs -f below the top level.

Acceptance criteria:
- sync is idempotent: running it twice produces no diff
- gitfriend doctor exits zero afterwards
- an env grep for GH_TOKEN and GITEA_TOKEN is empty in a fresh shell
result:
sync done. 69 tests pass, clippy clean. Generated from the real machine config into a scratchpad; NOTHING in HOME was written.

gitfriend sync generates the includeIf rules that select an identity per repository. Reports and stops by default; --write applies. Re-running compares before writing, so "already up to date" is honest and mtimes stay put.

KEY DESIGN DECISION, a change from the original plan: sync writes ONLY into its own directory and never parses or rewrites hand-maintained config. The plan called for generating into per-account gitconfigs plus a marked region inside gitconfig-common. Instead adoption is one include line added once, pointing at includes.gitconfig. That boundary removes the whole class of problems the plan worried about - no marked region to preserve, no merge to get wrong, idempotency is trivial, and uninstalling is deleting a directory and one line.

Path rules are emitted BEFORE URL rules: git applies includes in order and last match wins, so the remote (better evidence) overrides a directory guess. Path rules only decide for repos with no remote.

TWO BUGS THE PREVIEW CAUGHT, both of which would have failed SILENTLY:

1. The scp-style user is not always git. Digilope remotes look like gitea-at-app-gitea.digilope.com colon daniel/..., and a literal git-at pattern misses them entirely - the repo falls back to the default identity with no error. Now wildcarded to star-at.

2. Double-star only spans separators when it FOLLOWS one. Directly after the colon in an scp URL it degrades to a single star, so a host-wide pattern never reached org/repo. Measured against git 2.50.1: host colon double-star does NOT match, host colon star slash double-star DOES. Both spellings are now emitted.

The test that caught the second one asks REAL GIT which identity it selects for a real scp remote, rather than asserting on generated text - asserting on text only proves we wrote what we meant to write.

doctor gained a check for an account with no author name, after sync was observed generating an empty name field, which would make every commit in that repo fail.

Verification evidence:
- identity file per account with name and email. PASS
- sshcommand pinned only for accounts declaring a key; an account without one does not inherit anothers. PASS
- one account pattern expands to every URL form git might see. PASS
- declared paths become gitdir rules. PASS
- path rules precede URL rules. PASS
- generating twice is byte-identical, and a second write reports already up to date. PASS
- every generated file carries a generated-by header. PASS
- REAL GIT selects the Digilope identity for the scp remote with a non-git user. PASS after fix

NOT done, all cutover work: nothing written to HOME; the include line not added; credential.useHttpPath not set; the url-scoped github.com helper in gitconfig-darwin (currently gh auth git-credential) not displaced.

Unrelated observation: a commit from another Claude Code session landed in this repo mid-work, removing the target.noindex ignore entry. No conflict - my work sits cleanly on top, nothing lost, and target.noindex remains ignored via the global excludes file.

name: gitfriend: repo-based identity and credential selection
description:
Epic. Build a Rust binary that selects the correct git identity and per-provider credentials from the repository itself, wherever it lives on disk, with no ambient tokens in the shell environment.

Replaces the current path-based machinery (includeIf gitdir: rules + direnv GH_TOKEN export), which resolves silently wrong for relocated clones and leaks every token into every direnv-managed directory.

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-gitfriend-design.md
Requirements: REQUIREMENTS.md (R1-R15)

Key decisions: Rust binary + generated shell glue; least-privilege by default with an opt-in shell-env escape hatch; macOS Keychain behind a pluggable backend trait; GitHub + Gitea/Forgejo + GitLab + Azure DevOps in v1; MCP servers wrapped via gitfriend exec; origin wins on multi-remote; path fallback then declared default for remote-less repos; single accounts.toml generates the gitconfigs.

Done when: git, gh, tea and provider MCP servers all authenticate as the right account from any location, an env grep for GH_TOKEN is empty, and gitfriend doctor reports no drift.

name: Rotate tokens where the provider has an API for it
description:
UNVERIFIED LEADS - confirm against current docs before planning.

The providers differ in kind here, not just in endpoint, which is the interesting part:

- GITLAB is believed to have a genuine rotation endpoint that issues a replacement and revokes the predecessor in one call. If so it is the cleanest case and the one to build first, since the atomicity is handled server-side.
- GITEA / FORGEJO (so also Codeberg) can create tokens over the API using basic auth, so rotation is create-new then delete-old. Not atomic, which means gitfriend has to sequence it safely.
- AZURE DEVOPS has, or had, a PAT lifecycle API in preview. Preview APIs move; check whether it is still there.
- GITHUB deliberately offers no API to mint a PAT. That is a design stance, not a gap, and it is why the GitHub case gets its own task.

The safe sequence for any non-atomic provider, and the part worth getting right:
1. mint the replacement
2. VERIFY it works, with a real authenticated call
3. only then store it, replacing the old value
4. only then revoke the predecessor
Failing between 1 and 3 leaves an orphaned token, which is untidy. Failing after 4 with an unverified replacement locks you out. So verification must sit before the store, and revocation last.

This also needs a decision about what rotation means for a shared variable: three accounts declare GH_TOKEN but each has its own value, so rotation is per (account, variable), which the store is already keyed by.

Acceptance: one provider rotates end to end, the new token authenticates, the old one no longer does, and an interrupted rotation leaves a working credential in place.

name: Secret backends: Keychain + env, with migration
description:
Pluggable secret storage behind a trait: Backend { get, set, delete, fingerprint }.

Backends:
- keychain.rs - macOS Keychain. Only secret store installed on this machine (security(1); no op, pass or age).
- env.rs - reads GH_TOKEN_<Account> style vars. Retained for migration and CI, not as the default.

CLI: gitfriend secret set|list|delete. list shows fingerprints only, never values (R10). No value may ever appear in output, logs, or error messages.

Migration: import the existing plaintext exports from ~/.zshrc.local into the Keychain - GH_TOKEN_DanielCarmingham, GH_TOKEN_DanielAtProfound, GH_TOKEN_DanielAtKitchenCloud, GITEA_TOKEN. Leave GITEA_HOST as a literal in accounts.toml (non-secret). Do NOT remove GITHUB_PAT or GITHUB_PAT_PROFOUND yet - they have no known consumer and are handled separately.

Risk: Keychain prompts on every helper invocation would violate R15. Verify the ACL grants the gitfriend binary persistent access, and re-test after each rebuild since a changed binary signature can re-trigger prompts.

Acceptance criteria:
- set then get round-trips through the Keychain with no interactive prompt on the second call
- list output contains fingerprints and no token material
- a hyperfine run of the resolve path stays in single-digit milliseconds (R15)
result:
Delivered the backend layer. Scope narrowed: the secret CLI and the zshrc.local import moved to a follow-up task, because both need CLI dispatch which arrives with the credential helper. 17 tests pass, clippy clean.

Three backends behind one Backend trait { get, set, delete }:
- AgeFileBackend - all secrets in one age-encrypted file, unlocked by an x25519 identity key. The working default.
- KeychainBackend - platform credential store. Implemented, but NOT usable yet, see below.
- EnvBackend - read-only reader for the existing GH_TOKEN_<Account> scheme, so migration is a copy rather than a token re-issue. Writing through it errors rather than pretending to store.

KEY FINDING - the Keychain acceptance criterion FAILED, and it is the reason the default changed. macOS keys a Keychain ACL to the calling binarys designated requirement, which for an unsigned binary is its code hash. Wrote an entry with one build, rebuilt, read with the next: it blocked indefinitely on a GUI prompt and had to be killed. Same-binary round trips fine in 0.06s; it is specifically the rebuild that breaks it. Since the credential helper runs on every git transport operation, that fails R15 outright. Signing the installed binary with a stable identity should fix it - the machine has a valid Apple Development identity - but codesign then blocked on its own prompt for the signing key, so this is PLAUSIBLE AND UNVERIFIED. examples/keychain_probe.rs reproduces the whole thing.

SECOND FINDING - ages passphrase mode costs 1.53s per read because scrypt is deliberately expensive. Switched to an x25519 identity, which removes the KDF: read cost dropped below a millisecond and the suite went from 3.05s to 0.00s. A regression test now pins reads under 100ms so a KDF cannot creep back in.

Design decisions recorded:
- Secrets keyed by account AND variable, not one secret per account. An account can hold several credentials, and a checker can name exactly which one is missing. This drops the separate secret field the design doc had.
- Absence is not an error. get returns None when nothing is stored so a caller can distinguish "no value" from "the store broke"; conflating them is how a missing credential becomes a silent fallback.

Verification evidence:
- age backend round-trips a value. PASS
- the encrypted file contains neither the token value nor the variable name in plaintext, asserted by reading the raw bytes back. PASS
- read stays under 100ms. PASS, sub-millisecond in practice
- fingerprint neither contains the secret nor appears inside it, and is stable and distinguishing. PASS
- env backend reads VAR_Account. PASS
- keychain same-binary round trip and delete. PASS, run explicitly with --ignored so cargo test never blocks on a GUI prompt
- keychain across-rebuild read. FAIL, hangs on prompt, documented above

Honest note: secrets and identity files are written 0600, but an identity key on disk means anything that can read it can decrypt the store. Encryption defends the file at rest - backups, sync folders, an accidental commit - not against a local process. The cross-project exposure this project targets is solved by fetching on demand rather than exporting into the environment, which holds for either backend.

Cleaned up after testing: no gitfriend-selftest entries remain in the login keychain, verified with security dump-keychain.

commit.message: Add pluggable secret backends, defaulting to an encrypted file

name: secret CLI and migration import
description:
Split out of the secret-backends task, which delivered the backends but not the user-facing surface. Needs CLI dispatch, which arrives with the credential helper.

Work:
- gitfriend secret set|list|delete. list shows account, variable and FINGERPRINT only, never a value (R10).
- gitfriend secret init to generate the age identity file if absent.
- Backend selection: choose age file vs keychain vs env, defaulting to the age file until the keychain signing question is settled.
- Migration: import the existing plaintext exports from ~/.zshrc.local - GH_TOKEN_DanielCarmingham, GH_TOKEN_DanielAtProfound, GH_TOKEN_DanielAtKitchenCloud, GITEA_TOKEN. The env backend already reads that scheme, so this is a copy rather than a token re-issue. GITEA_HOST stays a literal in accounts.toml, not a secret. Do NOT remove GITHUB_PAT or GITHUB_PAT_PROFOUND - no consumer found, handled in the cutover task.

Acceptance criteria:
- secret list prints fingerprints and no token material, verified by grepping the output for a known value
- importing from the env backend and reading back through the age backend yields identical fingerprints
- the secrets file and the identity file are both mode 0600
result:
Secret CLI done. 37 tests pass, clippy clean.

gitfriend secret init | set | list | delete | import --from-env.

SECURITY DECISION: set reads the value from STDIN and never accepts it as an argument. Anything in argv is readable by every process on the machine via ps, which would undo the point of storing it encrypted. set also strips a trailing newline - one arriving from echo or a heredoc would be transmitted as part of the token and rejected by the server with an error that says nothing about whitespace.

DESIGN DECISION: list enumerates what the CONFIG DECLARES rather than what the store happens to contain. A declared variable with no stored value shows as MISSING, which is exactly the drift a checker exists to surface (R12), and it avoids adding enumeration to the Backend trait - awkward to implement for a keychain. Literal VAR=value entries are excluded, since GITEA_HOST carries its own value and is not a secret.

Added Account::secret_vars() to config, shared by list, import, and later by doctor: bare env entries plus gitCredential, deduplicated, literals excluded.

import --from-env copies from the GH_TOKEN_<Account> scheme the machine already uses, so migration is a copy rather than a token re-issue. It reads the running process environment, so it must be run from a shell that has those exports loaded - worth remembering since ~/.zshrc.local is only sourced for interactive shells.

Verification evidence, all against the real binary:
- set from stdin then list shows the correct fingerprint. PASS
- list output contains no token material even after storing one. PASS, R10
- a declared variable with no value is reported MISSING, and GITEA_HOST (a literal) is not listed as a secret. PASS
- identity.key and secrets.age are both mode 0600. PASS
- import --from-env preserves values exactly: fingerprints of the imported tokens match fingerprints of the source values. PASS
- manual smoke run confirms the stored token does not appear in secrets.age, checked by grepping the file.

NOT done: importing this machines REAL tokens. That is a live-machine action and belongs with the cutover, so it has not been performed. Nothing on this machine has been changed.

name: Cutover, docs, and loose ends
description:
THE RUNBOOK IS docs/CUTOVER.md IN THE REPO. Read it first; it has the full step-by-step with a verification and an undo for each step. This entry is just the index.

Starting config: docs/accounts.toml.example - match patterns already derived from every origin remote under ~/Developer, so the org scan does not need redoing.

Order (ambient tokens come out LAST, after their replacement is proven, so there is never a window with neither):
1. Install the release binary to a STABLE path first - shims and wrapped MCP commands bake in the path of the binary that generated them
2. accounts.toml + secret init + secret import --from-env (must run in an INTERACTIVE shell; zshrc.local is only sourced there)
3. sync --write, then add ONE include line to .gitconfig-common
4. Take over git credentials: useHttpPath true for github.com, and replace the URL-SCOPED helper in .gitconfig-darwin, which currently points at gh auth git-credential. This is the riskiest step - it is what makes git push work today.
5. shim install for gh and tea, shim dir early on PATH
6. mcp sync --write for Digilope/one-drop-visuals - the live exposure
7. Remove the ambient tokens: direnvrc account block, account-root .envrc exports, envrc.local
8. Commit to the cfg repo and rewrite ~/ACCOUNTS.md

Still to decide, detailed in the runbook: whether to declare patterns for the ~12 third-party clones or leave them Unmatched; whether to delete the now-duplicate tokens from ~/.zshrc.local; what consumes GITHUB_PAT and GITHUB_PAT_PROFOUND; and whether signing the binary makes the Keychain backend viable.

Verification gate throughout: gitfriend doctor exits non-zero on any problem and never writes.

name: Git credential helper
description:
Implement gitfriend credential get|store|erase speaking the git credential helper protocol. Highest-value single piece: it alone satisfies R1/R2/R3 for git transport, with zero dependence on filesystem path.

Verified on this machine (git 2.50.1) and load-bearing:
- The helper runs with cwd set to the repo worktree.
- GIT_DIR is NOT exported to the helper (only GIT_PREFIX, GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_EDITOR, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS), so resolution must ask git from cwd.
- With credential.useHttpPath=true, a fill for https://github.com/EJ-Rice/somerepo.git yields path=EJ-Rice/somerepo.git. The org is in the request, so the account resolves at CLONE time, before any repo exists on disk.

Requires setting credential.useHttpPath = true for github.com so the org reaches the helper. This replaces GCM for github.com, so the existing credential stack in ~/.gitconfig-common needs untangling first: it currently sets helper four times, including two empty resets.

Risk control: keep GCM configured for non-github hosts, and stage this behind a per-host override so it reverts with one config line.

Acceptance criteria:
- git clone of an https repo under each GitHub account authenticates as that account, from a directory outside every account root
- an ssh account (Digilope) is untouched: no token defined, push/pull works via core.sshcommand (R7)
- a missing secret produces a non-zero exit and no fallback token (R8)
result:
Credential helper and CLI dispatch done. 26 tests pass, clippy clean.

gitfriend credential get|store|erase speaks git protocol on stdin/stdout. get resolves the account from the request URL, falling back to the working directory only when git sent too little to identify a host. store and erase are deliberate no-ops: gitfriend own store is the source of truth, and letting git cache a copy elsewhere would put the same token in a second place under different access rules (R11).

CLI dispatch added via clap, with GITFRIEND_CONFIG / GITFRIEND_SECRETS / GITFRIEND_IDENTITY overriding the default ~/.config/gitfriend paths so tests never touch the real machine.

NEW SCHEMA FIELD: gitCredential names which declared variable holds the git password. Explicit rather than inferred from provider - an account may hold several credentials and guessing which is the password is implicit behaviour that fails quietly. ssh accounts omit it and are never handed a token.

R8 HOLE FOUND AND FIXED, discovered by writing the test for it. When git sent no host, resolution fell through to the working directory and could land on the declared default, releasing that account token. The test caught it releasing personal-token. The credential path now refuses on a Default resolution. The default is still fine for identity - committing as your usual self in a scratch repo is harmless - but it is not a basis for releasing a credential.

Verification evidence, end-to-end tests drive REAL git against the REAL release binary, not a mock of the protocol:
- git credential fill returns Work token for a WorkOrg URL. PASS
- same command, same cwd, Personal URL returns Personal token. PASS, this is R3
- STANDING INSIDE A REPO BELONGING TO Personal, a WorkOrg URL returns Work token. PASS. Anything keyed on filesystem location answers Personal here. This is R1/R2 demonstrated rather than argued.
- unclaimed host: git exits non-zero and stdout contains no token. PASS, R11
- missing secret: refuses, error names account and variable, carries no token material. PASS, R8
- ssh account is never handed a token and is not required to declare one. PASS, R7
- low-confidence Default resolution refuses. PASS, R8

R15 MEASURED on the release binary, n=100 with warmup:
- bare process spawn baseline (/usr/bin/true): 5.05 ms
- gitfriend credential get: 5.20 ms
- gitfriend own work: 0.15 ms
Comfortably inside budget. An earlier 17 ms reading was shell loop overhead in the measurement harness, not the binary - re-measured in-process to isolate it.

NOT done here: credential.useHttpPath=true must be set for github.com for the org to reach the helper, and the existing ~/.gitconfig-common credential stack needs untangling first (it sets helper four times including two empty resets). That is live-machine work and belongs to the sync/doctor and cutover tasks. Nothing on this machine has been changed.

name: Stretch goals
description:
Not required for the project to be done. Parked here so they stop occupying working memory.

Everything under this is blocked on the cutover: rotating a credential is only meaningful once gitfriend is the thing that holds credentials.

Common thread: the secret store already does set/get/delete, and doctor already reports per-account/per-variable state by fingerprint. Rotation is mostly provider adapters plus one piece of metadata (expiry) the store does not carry yet.

IMPORTANT: the provider API details in the child tasks are LEADS, recalled rather than verified. Check each against current docs before planning work on it - several of these APIs changed recently and one of them may not exist in the form described.
